notes:
T311 — fixed two defects in tools/runner:

1. DARWIN WALKER NOISE (primary). The runner probed _descendant_pids_linux on every poll (250 ms), caught FileNotFoundError on darwin, fell back to ps — and printed the fallback notice every time. Measured ratio from live evidence (untracked/oracle-v2-rebuild-2026-08-03.log): 13,785 fallback lines vs 173 progress/sweep lines (98.8% noise). Fix: platform detection once at startup via _detect_walker(), stored in _WALKER_FN/_WALKER_NAME module-level constants; walker choice reported once as '[runner] process walker: ps (darwin)'.

2. PREPEND_RELEASEFAST OPTIMIZE DETECTION. prepend_releasefast() checked '-Doptimize' in argv using exact token equality, which never matches '-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe' (it's a single token with an embedded '='). So the caller's flag was not detected and -Doptimize=ReleaseFast was injected anyway, making it impossible to produce ReleaseSafe/Debug builds through the sanctioned path. Fix: detect any argv element that starts with -Doptimize (or is exactly -O). Reproduced before fix: 'zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe' → argv = 'zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe ...'; after fix: '-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe' passes through.

ADDITIONAL CHANGES:
- Rate-limiting: added _runner_print() dedup helper — suppresses consecutive identical [runner] lines, so the next per-poll message added cannot recreate this class of noise.
- --log-rss cadence: throttled to at most once per 2 seconds (was every poll at 250 ms). Stated plainly in brief acceptance.

CONTROLS (tools/regression-runner-reporting.sh, wired into zig build test):
- Null: walker line count == 1, peak RSS reported without --log-rss
- Seeded (noise): zero 'linux walker failed' lines on darwin (SKIP on Linux)
- Seeded (optimize): ReleaseSafe survives without ReleaseFast injection
- Guard bite: RSS cap 50 MB kills (exit 124) and reports why

All five smoke tests passed on darwin (2026-08-03). Regression test passes all four arms.

Did not check:
- Linux /proc walker path (no Linux host available) — code path is unchanged except for the once-at-startup detection
- Whether the optimise-mode fix interacts with the --no-prepend-zig flag (it doesn't — --no-prepend-zig skips the entire prepend_releasefast call)
